title: The Greek gift
line: The bishop sacrifice on h7 (or h2), followed by the knight and the queen.

steps.text: Black has castled, and no knight guards h7. Your bishop, knight and queen are close, and the pawn on h4 will back the knight.
Give the bishop: take the pawn in front of the king, with check.
steps.hint: Your bishop already aims at it.
steps.after: The king took the bishop. Declining it comes at the end of the lesson.

steps.text: Check with the knight. The pawn on h4 guards it.
steps.after: Black's best try: the king steps forward to h6.

steps.text: Move your other knight off the bishop's diagonal. Then the knight on g5 can move with discovered check.

also.d2b3: That clears the diagonal too. This lesson goes on with the other knight move.
also.d2c4: That clears the diagonal too. This lesson goes on with the other knight move.

steps.hint: One of your knights stands between your bishop and the black king.
steps.after: Black took the knight, and the bishop's line to the king is open.

steps.text: Now jump with the knight: the bishop gives check, and the knight attacks the queen.
steps.after: Discovered check, and the queen is attacked.
The bishop and knight given up have come back as a queen.

steps.text: If the king had gone back to the corner instead, bring the queen next to the knight. She threatens mate.
steps.after: Black can only stop the mate by giving up material.

steps.text: If Black does not take the bishop at all, step it back to safety: you are a pawn up and the king has lost its cover.

summary: Bishop takes the pawn beside the castled king with check, the knight checks behind it, and the other pieces join in.
